label: copy-phase input x (fed-back x, not the first original token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is x, i.e. the model has just emitted x and it is fed back. It never fires on x during the original phase or on the delimiter. When the fed-back x is original token 0 (recall_idx 1) it fires rarely and weakly (about 0.1 of max), so the predicate excludes that case. Magnitude is largest for a single x copied mid-sequence; a second consecutive x fires much more weakly than the first. Rate rises somewhat with L. About 13% of predicate-true steps are inactive, mostly short sequences or the last few outputs. Does not depend on which token is being output.

issues: Minor: recall_idx==1 (the fed-back x is original token 0) is not 'rare'. Precision there is 0.24 on test, so it fires about a quarter of the time, though weakly (2.8% of mass). Leaving it out is still the right call.
Minor: the second of two consecutive x's still fires often (precision 0.74). It is weaker but not usually silent; it carries 1.8% of mass.

The inactive true-predicate steps are concentrated in short sequences: precision is 0.34 at L=3 and 0.65 at L=4, versus 0.89 at L>=7. Requiring L>=4 only moves test F1 from 0.905 to 0.905, so this is not worth adding.
Small overclaim: 'magnitude highest mid-sequence'. Several top examples (around 0.96 of max) are x at the final output step (to_go=0).

Checked and confirmed: zero activations in the original phase or on the delimiter, and zero on any input token other than x. Rates are flat across out_tok and next_out, consistent with 'no dependence on output token'. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.870, R 0.943, F1 0.905 and mass recall 0.972, versus F1 0.860 for plain copy-phase x. Misses are only at recall_idx 1 and are low-magnitude.
